leaderboards.title: Best AI coding agents
leaderboards.note: Scored tools ran our standard task between 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-26 (see the test write-up). The AI model differs between tools (Copilot: gpt-6-luna, Cursor CLI: Composer 2.5, Aider, Cline, Crush, Goose, Pi and Qwen Code: gemini-3.8-flash, Bolt.new: its Free-plan default, OpenCode: its built-in free deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, Kilo Code: Kilo's Auto Free model, which picked reflection/beam), and the model affects the score, so treat cross-tool comparisons with care. Tied scores are listed alphabetically. Untested tools are listed alphabetically below. Pricing facts checked on official sites on 2026-10-15/16 (OpenCode on 2026-10-19, Crush on 2026-10-20, Goose on 2026-10-21, Pi on 2026-10-22, Qwen Code on 2026-10-23, Kilo Code on 2026-10-26).

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.description: GitHub's AI coding assistant and agent for editors, the CLI and pull requests.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 38 s with no interventions on Copilot Free. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label always says 'Mark as complete', even for completed tasks.

tools.name: Pi
tools.pricing: Free, open source (MIT); you pay for your own model API usage
tools.description: Minimal, extensible open-source terminal coding agent (read, bash, edit and write tools, plus extensions, skills and print/JSON/RPC modes); works with many model providers.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 50 s with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote all four files in 6 model requests, then a 7th request (a quick self-check) hit the free tier's per-minute request limit and Pi stopped without retrying, so there was no final summary. Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, labelled input, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state, correct README. -1 DX: needs Node 22.19+ (one extra step on our Node 20 machine). -1 DX: no final summary and no retry after the rate-limit error.

tools.name: Crush
tools.pricing: Free, source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT); you pay for your own model API usage (Charm's own Hyper provider has a free tier but needs sign-in)
tools.description: Charm's open terminal coding agent (Crush CLI) that works with many model providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter and more).

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 646 s (17 model requests, no interventions) on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote its own Node test, caught and fixed a counter bug before finishing. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label is always 'Mark task complete'. -1 speed: took about 11 minutes (slow model responses). -1 DX: short final summary and a .crush/ data folder left in the project. Checker note: the original checker missed the counter because the number and label are separate flex items; checker v1.1 fixes this for every tool (all earlier scores unchanged).

tools.name: Cursor
tools.description: AI-first code editor with an agent that can plan, edit and run code across your project.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 37 s with 1 prompt and no interventions on a free Cursor account (the web Cloud Agents need Premium; the CLI did not). -1 quality: task IDs use crypto.randomUUID(), which fails outside secure contexts (e.g. plain http on a LAN IP). -1: the checkbox accessibility label is always 'Mark task complete'. -1 DX: separate browser login step.

tools.name: Kilo Code
tools.pricing: Free, open source (MIT) for individuals; free models via Auto Free with no account, or pay as you go, bring your own key, or Kilo Pass; Teams $15/user/month
tools.description: Open-source agentic coding assistant for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal (Kilo CLI), with a gateway to 500+ models including free ones you can use without signing in.

test.model: Kilo Auto Free (routed to reflection/beam; no account, no API key)
test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 11 s with no interventions, no sign-in, no API key and no card, using Kilo's Auto Free model (which picked reflection/beam on test day). -1 quality: an unused escapeHtml helper left in the code. -1: the checkbox has no accessible label. -1: the delete button just says 'Delete' and doesn't name the task. -1 DX: the final summary was just 'Done.'. Note: Auto Free chooses the model for you and can change over time, and Kilo says it may route to providers that log prompts, so don't use it for private code.

tools.name: Cline
tools.pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage)
tools.description: Open-source autonomous coding agent that runs inside VS Code.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks. First attempt hit Gemini high demand (no files); re-run completed the app in 312 s (then hit the free-tier 20-request/day quota after Cline's own self-test passed, before a final summary). Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent escaping, dynamic aria-labels. Speed −3 for the high-demand re-run. DX −2: no final summary because of quota.

tools.name: Aider
tools.pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage)
tools.description: Open-source AI pair programmer that edits code in your local git repo from the terminal.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 26 s (1 model request, no interventions). -3 quality: README cut off and 2 stray files created from README code snippets. -3 DX: pip install failed on Python 3.13 (worked with Python 3.12) and the stray files.

tools.name: Bolt.new
tools.referral_note: Referral link: we may earn a commission and you get 20% off; it never affects scores or rankings.
tools.description: Browser-based AI app builder that generates, runs and deploys full-stack web apps from prompts.

test.tool_version: Bolt.new web app (Free plan, Standard mode)
test.model: Bolt.new default model (Free plan; model name not shown)
test.evidence: Passed 10/10 checks in about 2 minutes with 1 prompt and no interventions on the Free plan. 9 checks verified in Bolt's live preview; the reload/persistence check (C8) was verified on the exported project because the preview did not come back after a page reload. -2 quality: left Vite starter files (package.json, package-lock.json, .bolt) and an unused escapeHtml function. -2: no accessibility labels on the input, checkbox or icon-only delete button. -2 DX: the preview showed a stale starter page until refreshed and broke on reload.

tools.name: Goose
tools.pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage
tools.description: Open-source, extensible AI agent (desktop app, CLI and API) from the Agentic AI Foundation, originally built by Block; works with many model providers.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. All four files were written within 18.5 minutes (6 model requests), but Gemini 'high demand' errors and slow responses meant Goose had not posted its final reply when our 20-minute timebox ended, so we scored the files present at the cutoff and counted the full 20 minutes. Quality 25: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state. -5 speed: 20 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: no final summary before the cutoff.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.pricing: Free, open source; free models included, or bring your own model provider
tools.description: Open-source AI coding agent for the terminal, IDE and desktop, with built-in free models.

test.model: deepseek-v4.1-flash-free (OpenCode built-in free model, no account)
test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks; the successful run took 20 s with no sign-in and no card. First try on the big-pickle free model returned 'Rate limit exceeded', so we re-ran on another built-in free model (counts as 1 intervention, -3 speed). -1 quality: README says to visit localhost:8000 after 'npx serve .', which serves on port 3000. -1: the checkbox accessibility label is always 'Mark task complete'. -2 DX: with no model set it auto-picked a provider it had no credentials for (an unrelated Cloudflare token on our test machine), and 'opencode run' hung when stdin was left open; the final summary was one line.

tools.name: Qwen Code
tools.pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage (the free Qwen OAuth tier ended 2026-04-15)
tools.description: Open-source terminal coding agent from Alibaba's Qwen team (originally forked from Gemini CLI); works with OpenAI-, Anthropic- and Gemini-compatible providers and has a headless mode for scripts and CI.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier and ended with a clear summary, but took 18 minutes: Gemini was slow and returned 6 'high demand' errors (Qwen Code retried them itself), and the agent spent 4 extra requests reading files that did not exist yet. Quality 23: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, correct README. -1 the text input has no label (placeholder only); -1 checkbox and delete labels don't name the task. -4 speed: 18 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: needs Node 22+ and a hand-written settings file to use a Gemini key headlessly.

attempts.note: Retest of Goose CLI 1.56.0 on gemini-3.8-flash. The first model reply took 504 s, then the Gemini free tier returned three 503 errors and Goose exited with a network error before writing any files. Not a fair test, so no new score.

Planned retests on a quieter Gemini day. Three 1-token test requests to gemini-3.8-flash on the free tier between 04:02 and 04:11 CDT got no answer (timed out after 120, 90 and 60 seconds), so we didn't start either run.

new_this_week.name: Hob
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) desktop app that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss on your own computer, as an offline, private alternative to Claude and ChatGPT; no account or subscription. FrigadeHQ/hob; Show HN Oct 26 (144 pts), v0.2 released Oct 26. Mac, Windows, Linux.

new_this_week.name: desigma
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT/Apache-2.0), offline Figma alternative written in Rust, with a local MCP server so coding agents can inspect designs, edit them and generate code; imports Figma files. Early alpha (first release Oct 11); Product Hunt #9 on Oct 26.

new_this_week.name: GEOInflow
new_this_week.description: Self-hosted analytics (MIT) that shows which AI crawlers and AI search engines visit your site, which pages they request or miss, and what traffic AI search sends you. Open-sourced Oct 26, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Corgi
new_this_week.description: Terminal multiplexer for humans and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode): shows which agent is working or needs you, keeps sessions running like tmux, tracks tokens and file changes. MIT (tals/corgi); Show HN Oct 23 (138 pts). macOS, Linux, WSL.

new_this_week.name: Farol
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source CLI and GitHub Action that maps the risk of a pull request after AI review: riskiest files, what they reach, diff coverage and contract breaks (TS/React, Go, Python). MIT (winnin/farol); Show HN Oct 25.

new_this_week.name: AgentValley
new_this_week.description: Free macOS notch app that shows every Claude Code session and sub-agent at a glance (model, working or waiting on you), each with a pixel programmer. MIT (morsechimwai/agent-valley); Product Hunt #4 on Oct 24.

new_this_week.name: tstack (Theo / t3dotgg)
new_this_week.description: Theo's everyday agent skills for Claude Code and Codex: full-send PR flow, multi-model 'council' review, babysit-PR through CI, take over someone else's PR. MIT; published Oct 24. Needs an authenticated gh CLI.

new_this_week.name: BeautifulRust
new_this_week.description: Claude Code plugin that teaches Claude to write idiomatic, robust Rust. MIT; created Oct 23, 900+ stars in its first days.

new_this_week.name: xss-audit skill
new_this_week.description: Agent skill that runs a 14-layer static XSS audit on React, TypeScript and JavaScript projects. MIT; created Oct 24. A useful second check on AI-written front-end code.

new_this_week.name: Halv
new_this_week.description: Desktop workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex, Kimi and GLM side by side on the plans you already pay for, with a local proxy that trims context tokens and a live savings meter. The app and its local engine went open source (Apache-2.0) on Oct 22; only the optional Halv Cloud router is paid. macOS first; Show HN Oct 22.

new_this_week.name: Recursive Flint + rec
new_this_week.description: Flint is a local coding model from Recursive with open weights on Hugging Face (Apache-2.0); rec is its Apache-2.0 inference engine with ready-made launchers for Pi and OpenCode. Needs an Apple Silicon M4 Pro/M5 Pro/M5 Max with 48 GB+ memory. Released Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Rossark Motion skill
new_this_week.description: Claude Code skill that turns any SVG drawing into a smooth 60 fps animation (breathing, blinking, full-body acting, whole scenes) in React Native and SwiftUI. Handy for app and game illustrations. MIT; created Oct 22, trending on GitHub.

new_this_week.name: 3D Model Anything (Wes Bos)
new_this_week.description: iPhone LiDAR + photo capture app, a Three.js viewer and a scan-to-threejs agent skill that guides a coding agent through rebuilding a real room as an editable 3D scene. Good fit for game devs and Three.js tinkerers. Code MIT (demo assets under a separate license); created Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Omnara
new_this_week.description: Open-source, self-hostable server for durable agents: create an agent with an API call and Omnara runs the loop, sandboxes, secrets and permissions, with state in Postgres so agents survive restarts. Your laptop or a cloud sandbox can join as a machine. Apache-2.0; hosted version at omnara.com. Show HN Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Harp
new_this_week.description: Unofficial fork of the Warp terminal with a sidebar for running many Claude Code and Codex sessions side by side: shows which agent is working, waiting for you or done, plus usage-limit rings. macOS, free, AGPL-3.0. Created Oct 20, trending on GitHub.

new_this_week.name: durable-harness (Vercel)
new_this_week.description: Runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi or your own coding agent as a durable session that logs every model and tool call and resumes after crashes or timeouts. Open source (Apache-2.0) from Vercel Labs; announced Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: BAND for Developers
new_this_week.description: Shared chat rooms where coding agents and people collaborate, with governance over how agents talk to each other. Free plan for personal, non-commercial use (up to 20 remote agents); Pro $17.99/mo. Product Hunt #2 on Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: SuperCMO AI
new_this_week.description: Open-source agent skills that turn Claude Code, Cursor or Codex into a marketing team for your product: learns your brand, studies competitor ads, writes copy and makes UGC, product and image ads, asking before anything expensive renders. Apache-2.0; bring your own model keys or pay per use. Product Hunt Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Opposable
new_this_week.description: Free Android app that lets Claude, ChatGPT or Codex operate your phone's apps, with an on-device 2B screen model (GUI-Owl 1.5, 1.5 GB download) as an offline fallback. Show HN Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Reticle
new_this_week.description: Makes your coding agent verify its own work: drives the running app, reads network calls, state and console, and returns pass/fail/cannot tell with the file:line to fix. SDK Apache-2.0, server source-available (FSL); free to start, no card. Show HN Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: fx0 (Vercel)
new_this_week.description: Vercel's open-source design agent: describe a page and it writes one HTML file, built on the durable libfx agent loop. Apache-2.0 (vercel-labs/fx0); hosted demo has a few free prompts, or self-host with your own AI Gateway.

new_this_week.name: Nimbalyst Wiki
new_this_week.description: A local markdown wiki your coding agents write and keep updated (decisions, open questions, the big picture). Free MIT plugin + MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP agents; no account. Product Hunt Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: MCP Census
new_this_week.description: Checks public evidence for an MCP server before you install it and returns PASS / REVIEW / BLOCK / UNKNOWN (a first gate, not a malware scan). 10 free lookups/day with no signup; free account 1,000 credits/month. Show HN Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: Pando
new_this_week.description: Self-hosted platform to deploy and share apps your team builds with AI, each behind access control from the start. Open source (AGPL-3.0); paid commercial license/hosting optional. Show HN Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: Triage by Chodeberg
new_this_week.description: Users file bug reports from their AI assistant into a live copy of your CLI/TUI/Linux app; Triage replays each on a clean machine and only forwards the ones that reproduce. Free 100 credits/month, then pay per minute. Product Hunt Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: Hermes GameForge
new_this_week.description: Game-dev plugin for the Hermes agent: generates SFX, music, NPC voices, sprites, tilesets and low-poly 3D models offline, scaffolds web/Godot/Unity builds and runs a playtester bot. MIT; brand-new (Oct 21) and not reviewed by us yet.

new_this_week.name: buddylist
new_this_week.description: Free desktop app (Mac, Windows, Linux) that puts Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and OpenCode in an MSN-style buddy list: group chats, separate Git worktrees, diffs and PR checks. Bring your own agent accounts. Product Hunt #8 and Show HN, Oct 19, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Craig
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) terminal UI that runs Claude Code, Codex and Cursor agents in parallel, each task in its own Git worktree, from task to PR. npm install, no account. Show HN, Oct 19, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Quorus
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) local relay where Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode agents join one room over MCP, fix in their own worktrees and review each other's work. Demo runs on free OpenCode models. Show HN, Oct 19, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Spotnote
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) Vite plugin: click any element in your running app, write what should change, and hand your coding agent the exact file, line and column. Local only, no account. Show HN, Oct 19, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Lights-on software factory
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) boilerplate for running Claude Code as a 'software factory': sandbox container, deterministic command regulator, linter hooks and a workflow generator that the author says cut token spend about 80%. Show HN, Oct 20, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Sphinx
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) git hook for agent-assisted coding: before you push, it quizzes you on what your AI agent's changes actually do. Show HN, Oct 18, 2026.

new_this_week.name: WhatsApp MCP (Cloudflare)
new_this_week.description: Open-source (MIT), read-only MCP server that lets your AI agent search and read your own WhatsApp messages; runs on Cloudflare Workers' free tier. Show HN, Oct 18, 2026.

new_this_week.name: llmspeed
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source web tool that simulates how fast a local LLM would run (tokens/sec, time to first token) on a given GPU or Mac before you buy hardware. Show HN, Oct 17, 2026.

new_this_week.name: withHuman
new_this_week.description: Open-source human approval layer for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, LangGraph and more). Intercepts tool calls; self-host or hosted. Product Hunt launch Oct 15, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Navige
new_this_week.description: Sits between agents and paid models/tools to cut runaway spend (routing, cache, loop guards). Free start. Product Hunt #2 on Oct 15, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Tiden
new_this_week.description: Intent verification for coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot). Specs versioned like code; 14-day free trial. Live with install script.

new_this_week.name: Graphicle
new_this_week.description: Local Rust code-graph + memory for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, MCP). No account. Apache-2.0. Show HN Oct 14, 2026.

new_this_week.name: OpenUI 1.0
new_this_week.description: Open standard for generative UI (React/Vue/Svelte/Angular runtimes). MIT on GitHub (thesysdev/openui). Useful for agent-built interfaces.
